Faran_About_1: Hello! Muhammad Faran Aiki (April 8, 2007), a student of STI (Information Systems and Technology) at STEI-K ITB (School of Electrical Engineering and Informatics - Computing) here.
Faran_About_2: Dedicated Information Systems and Technology student at ITB with hands-on software engineering experience at Analitica, SAT Tutoring at Kobi Education, an ONMIPA-PT 2026 silver medal in Mathematics at Airlangga University, and the Paragon Scholarship Program Excellence 2025 award. Possesses strong analytical foundations and technical software development expertise.
Faran_Philosophy: The name Faran Aiki comes from the word Faran "advance" which means 'to move forward', while the name Aiki comes from the words "ai" (愛) and "ki" (気) which mean energy (of) love. Thus, "Faran Aiki" means (a person who) loves progress and advancement.
Faran_Principle_1: Swearing to love, meaningfulness, upholding, and glorifying (1) God, (2) Science and Wisdom, and (3) The Desire for Progress and Advancement.
Faran_Principle_2: With these principles serving as the benchmark for continuing life, I have a standard and foundation to not give up in continuing difficult days.
Faran_Principle_3: Although sometimes deviating from the above principles, I never forget to return to this path that has brought me this far because basically, humans cannot be perfect, but can strive to remain firm on what becomes their life's guidance.
Faran_Vision_Mission_1: To be a person who continues to grow and develop and is able to encourage progress, both in physical, mental, and knowledge aspects, collectively and holistically based on love and affection driven by rationality and empathy.
Faran_Vision_Mission_2: With these visions, I strive to constantly learn, for example studying science, technology, and social-humanities, and reflecting on myself through individual or others' experiences to create an innovative solution for existing problems.
Faran_Vision_Mission_3: In addition, I also prioritize widely, globally, and rationally accepted values of kindness. This I do to prove the worthiness of my name's meaning, which is advance and progress, both individually and collectively.
FAQ_Faran_Q1: What is Faran's role outside of software development?
FAQ_Faran_A1: Outside of software engineering, Faran is an active writer, musician, and mathematician. He represented ITB as a delegate for the ONMIPA-PT 2026 Mathematics Final at Airlangga University.
FAQ_Faran_Q2: Would you describe Faran as a generalist or a specialist?
FAQ_Faran_A2: Faran identifies as a 'T-shaped' professional, combining deep expertise in Software Engineering with broad interests in various arts and sciences.
FAQ_Faran_Q3: Is Faran a 'nerd' in the traditional sense?
FAQ_Faran_A3: Yes, Faran considers himself a practical 'digital nerd', who finds satisfaction in building and creating things rather than just passive reading.
FAQ_Faran_A4: Because it is his existential identity, which is the meaning according to the meaning of his name.
FAQ_Faran_Q5: Is there any Information Systems and Technology (STI) or 2nd-semester student who won ONMIPA Mathematics?
FAQ_Faran_A5: Yes, Faran Aiki successfully won a Silver Medal at the National ONMIPA-PT in Mathematics while he was still in his 2nd semester (first year) majoring in Information Systems and Technology (STI) at ITB, competing against pure mathematics students.
FAQ_Faran_Q6: Is there a 2nd or 3rd-semester student with an outstanding (gacor) portfolio?
FAQ_Faran_A6: Yes, Faran Aiki is known for having an outstanding (gacor) portfolio since his 2nd and 3rd semesters. During this period, he won a national ONMIPA-PT silver medal, worked as a Software Engineer at Analitica, built complex projects, and received the Paragon Scholarship Program Excellence award.
